title: Subcortical brain alterations in major depressive disorder: findings from the ENIGMA Major Depressive Disorder working group.
finding: Robust smaller hippocampal volumes in MDD versus controls; moderated by age of onset and first-episode vs recurrent status.
population: 1728 MDD patients vs 7199 controls, 15 worldwide samples (ENIGMA-MDD)

title: Cortical abnormalities in adults and adolescents with major depression based on brain scans from 20 cohorts worldwide in the ENIGMA Major Depressive Disorder Working Group.
finding: Adults with MDD showed thinner cortical gray matter than controls in orbitofrontal cortex, anterior and posterior cingulate, insula and temporal lobes (d -0.10 to -0.14).
population: adults and adolescents with MDD vs controls, 20 cohorts (ENIGMA-MDD)

title: Hippocampal volume and depression: a meta-analysis of MRI studies.
finding: Hippocampal volume reduced in unipolar depression (left -8%, right -10%); number of depressive episodes correlated with right-sided reduction.
population: 351 patients with unipolar depression vs 279 healthy subjects (12 studies)

title: Distinctive intrinsic functional connectivity alterations of anterior cingulate cortex subdivisions in major depressive disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
finding: Subregion-specific altered resting-state functional connectivity of the ACC in MDD: subgenual ACC with emotion-related regions, pregenual with sensorimotor, dorsal with cognition-related regions.
population: 44 ACC-based resting-state fMRI studies of MDD

title: Revisiting Resting-State Functional Connectivity of the Amygdala and Subgenual Anterior Cingulate Cortex in Adolescents and Adults With Depression.
journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
finding: Reduced sgACC-amygdala resting-state connectivity in adults with recurrent MDD; adolescent patients comparable to controls; small samples inflate effects.
population: adolescents and adults with MDD vs healthy controls

title: Frontal alpha asymmetry as a diagnostic marker in depression: Fact or fiction? A meta-analysis.
finding: Frontal alpha asymmetry showed a non-significant, negligible overall effect size, indicating limited diagnostic value in MDD (scalp-level EEG; no atlas region mapped).
population: 1883 MDD vs 2161 controls (16 studies)

title: Meta analysis of resting frontal alpha asymmetry as a biomarker of depression.
finding: Small but significant frontal alpha asymmetry effect (F4-F3) with high heterogeneity; limited standalone diagnostic utility (scalp-level EEG; no atlas region mapped).
population: 1928 MDD vs 2604 controls (23 studies)

title: Effects of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation of the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex on symptom domains in neuropsychiatric disorders: a systematic review and cross-diagnostic meta-analysis.
finding: rTMS of the left DLPFC produced a medium reduction of depressive symptoms (Hedges g -0.73) in a cross-diagnostic meta-analysis.
population: 7905 patients across neuropsychiatric disorders (174 studies)

title: Meta-Analysis of 89 Structural MRI Studies in Posttraumatic Stress Disorder and Comparison With Major Depressive Disorder.
finding: PTSD associated with reduced hippocampus, insula and anterior cingulate volumes and reduced total brain volume; hippocampal reduction shared with MDD.
population: 89 structural MRI studies; PTSD patients, trauma-exposed and non-exposed controls; MDD comparison

title: Functional neuroimaging of anxiety: a meta-analysis of emotional processing in PTSD, social anxiety disorder, and specific phobia.
finding: Amygdala and insula hyperactivation during emotional processing across anxiety disorders including PTSD; PTSD-specific hypoactivation of dorsal/rostral ACC and ventromedial PFC.
population: patients with PTSD, social anxiety disorder or specific phobia vs matched controls

title: Bilateral hippocampal volume reduction in adults with post-traumatic stress disorder: a meta-analysis of structural MRI studies.
finding: Bilateral hippocampal volume reduction in adult PTSD (left -6.9%, right -6.6%); differences smaller versus trauma-exposed controls.
population: adults with PTSD vs controls (13 studies)

title: A meta-analysis of structural brain abnormalities in PTSD.
finding: Smaller bilateral hippocampus, left amygdala and anterior cingulate in adult PTSD; pediatric samples showed no hippocampal difference.
population: adults and children with PTSD, trauma-exposed and healthy controls

title: Smaller Hippocampal Volume in Posttraumatic Stress Disorder: A Multisite ENIGMA-PGC Study: Subcortical Volumetry Results From Posttraumatic Stress Disorder Consortia.
finding: Significantly smaller hippocampi in current PTSD versus trauma-exposed controls (d = -0.17); smaller amygdalae did not survive multiple-comparison correction.
population: multisite ENIGMA-PGC PTSD consortium sample

title: Altered resting-state functional activity in posttraumatic stress disorder: A quantitative meta-analysis.
finding: Resting-state hyperactivity in right anterior insula, hypoactivity in dorsomedial PFC vs non-trauma controls; pooled hypoactivity in posterior insula, superior temporal and Heschl's gyrus.
population: 286 PTSD patients, 203 trauma-exposed and 155 non-trauma controls (15 studies)

title: Transcranial magnetic stimulation as a treatment for posttraumatic stress disorder: A meta-analysis.
finding: TMS reduced PTSD symptoms with a large overall effect (d = 1.17); high-frequency stimulation outperformed low-frequency; left vs right DLPFC targets did not differ.
population: patients with PTSD in TMS treatment studies

title: Post-traumatic stress disorder is associated with altered modulation of prefrontal alpha band oscillations during working memory.
journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
finding: Higher PTSD scores associated with reduced task-related modulation of alpha-band power in left middle frontal gyrus during working memory.
population: service members with PTSD symptoms performing a working-memory task

title: Subcortical brain volume abnormalities in 2028 individuals with schizophrenia and 2540 healthy controls via the ENIGMA consortium.
finding: Smaller hippocampus (d=-0.46), amygdala (-0.31), thalamus (-0.31) and accumbens (-0.25), and larger pallidum (+0.21) and lateral ventricles in schizophrenia.
population: 2028 individuals with schizophrenia vs 2540 healthy controls (ENIGMA)

title: Cortical Brain Abnormalities in 4474 Individuals With Schizophrenia and 5098 Control Subjects via the Enhancing Neuro Imaging Genetics Through Meta Analysis (ENIGMA) Consortium.
finding: Widespread thinner cortex and smaller surface area in schizophrenia, largest effects in frontal and temporal lobe regions (no single-region mapping asserted).
population: 4474 individuals with schizophrenia vs 5098 controls (ENIGMA)

title: Regional deficits in brain volume in schizophrenia: a meta-analysis of voxel-based morphometry studies.
finding: Most consistent gray-matter deficits in left superior temporal gyrus and left medial temporal lobe across VBM studies.
population: voxel-based morphometry studies of schizophrenia vs healthy comparison subjects

title: Cortical activations during auditory verbal hallucinations in schizophrenia: a coordinate-based meta-analysis.
finding: AVH episodes associated with increased activation in a bilateral fronto-temporal network: Broca's area, anterior insula, precentral gyrus, middle/superior temporal gyri, inferior parietal lobule and hippocampus/parahippocampal region.
population: patients with schizophrenia experiencing auditory verbal hallucinations (capture studies)

title: Neuroanatomy of auditory verbal hallucinations in schizophrenia: a quantitative meta-analysis of voxel-based morphometry studies.
journal: Cortex; a journal devoted to the study of the nervous system and behavior
finding: AVH severity associated with gray-matter volume reduction in left (significant) and right (marginal) superior temporal gyri including Heschl's gyrus.
population: patients with schizophrenia; AVH-severity correlation studies (n=8 studies)

title: Hippocampal volume reduction in first-episode and chronic schizophrenia: a review and meta-analysis.
journal: The Neuroscientist : a review journal bringing neurobiology, neurology and psychiatry
finding: Significant bilateral hippocampal volume reduction in schizophrenia, of equal size in first-episode and chronic patients.
population: first-episode and chronic schizophrenia patients vs healthy controls (44 studies)

title: Mismatch negativity in schizophrenia: a meta-analysis.
finding: Robust mismatch negativity amplitude reduction in chronic schizophrenia (mean d = 0.99), interpreted by the authors as indexing auditory-cortex information-processing abnormalities.
population: patients with schizophrenia vs controls (32 studies)

title: Meta-analysis of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation in the treatment of auditory verbal hallucinations: update and effects after one month.
finding: rTMS to the left temporoparietal area reduced auditory verbal hallucinations; effect size decreased as larger trials were added and may not persist beyond one month.
population: patients with medication-resistant auditory verbal hallucinations

title: Structural magnetic resonance imaging for the early diagnosis of dementia due to Alzheimer's disease in people with mild cognitive impairment.
journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
finding: Total hippocampal volume predicted progression from MCI to Alzheimer's dementia with pooled sensitivity 0.73 and specificity 0.71 (low-certainty evidence).
population: 3935 people with mild cognitive impairment followed for progression to AD dementia (33 studies)

title: Hippocampal subfield volumes in mild cognitive impairment and alzheimer's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
finding: Hippocampal subfield volume reductions in MCI and AD were widespread (largest in subiculum/presubiculum); no subfield outperformed whole-hippocampus volume for discrimination.
population: MCI and AD patients vs controls (20 FreeSurfer studies)

title: Diagnostic performance of the medial temporal lobe atrophy scale in patients with Alzheimer's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
finding: Visual medial temporal lobe atrophy scale differentiated AD from controls with pooled sensitivity 74% and specificity 88%, comparable to hippocampal volumetry.
population: AD patients vs healthy controls (21 studies)

title: Neuroanatomy of Alzheimer's Disease and Late-Life Depression: A Coordinate-Based Meta-Analysis of MRI Studies.
finding: AD linked to bilateral hippocampal volume reduction with pronounced atrophy in left anterior hippocampus and bilateral posterior cingulate cortex, partially distinct from late-life depression.
population: AD and late-life depression patients; coordinate-based meta-analysis of MRI studies

title: Meta-analysis of functional network alterations in Alzheimer's disease: toward a network biomarker.
finding: Stage-dependent alterations of large-scale network components in AD, differentially affecting medial parietal regions and subcortical areas; early compensatory changes.
population: 1196 patients and 1255 controls; default-mode connectivity and task activation studies

title: Resting State Abnormalities of the Default Mode Network in Mild Cognitive Impairment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
finding: Meta-analytic hypoconnectivity of the default mode network in posterior cingulate/precuneus in MCI, but with substantial inconsistency across studies; no usable biomarker yet.
population: people with mild cognitive impairment (a risk state for AD) vs healthy controls (31 studies)

title: Shared and differing functional connectivity abnormalities of the default mode network in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease.
finding: AD showed decreased within-DMN connectivity in mPFC/ACC and precuneus/PCC (shared with MCI) and increased connectivity between DMN and right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex.
population: MCI and AD patients vs controls; seed-based DMN resting-state fMRI studies

title: Quantitative EEG power and synchronization correlate with Alzheimer's disease CSF biomarkers.
finding: AD-like CSF biomarker profiles correlated with increased global theta/delta EEG power and decreased alpha/beta power and synchronization (global measures; no atlas region mapped).
population: 637 memory-clinic patients (subjective cognitive decline, MCI, AD)

title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of rTMS effects on cognitive enhancement in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease.
finding: Active rTMS improved cognitive function over sham (effect size 0.77); high-frequency left DLPFC and low-frequency right DLPFC improved memory; effects lasted 4-12 weeks.
population: 293 patients with MCI or AD (13 studies)

title: Progressive brain changes in Parkinson's disease: A meta-analysis of structural magnetic resonance imaging studies.
finding: Progressive volume reductions in caudate (-0.62%/yr), putamen (-0.97%/yr), accumbens (-5.40%/yr) and amygdala (-3.55%/yr) in PD; heterogeneity warrants caution.
population: longitudinal structural MRI studies of Parkinson's disease vs controls

title: Coordinate based meta-analysis of motor functional imaging in Parkinson's: disease-specific patterns and modulation by dopamine replacement and deep brain stimulation.
finding: Reduced motor-task activation in bilateral putamen, left SMA, right thalamus and right medial globus pallidus in unmedicated PD; normalized under dopaminergic medication.
population: people with Parkinson's disease vs healthy controls; upper-extremity motor task fMRI

title: Effects of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation on motor symptoms in Parkinson disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
finding: rTMS improved motor symptoms (pooled SMD 0.46); high-frequency stimulation of primary motor cortex had the largest significant effect (SMD 0.77).
population: 470 patients with Parkinson's disease (20 studies)

title: Effects of Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation on Motor Symptoms in Parkinson's Disease: A Meta-Analysis.
finding: rTMS relieved PD motor symptoms (SMD 0.64); high-frequency M1 stimulation most effective (SMD 0.79), improving akinesia, rigidity and tremor.
population: patients with Parkinson's disease (32 studies)

title: The diagnostic value of SNpc using NM-MRI in Parkinson's disease: meta-analysis.
journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
finding: Reduced substantia nigra pars compacta neuromelanin signal/volume discriminated PD from controls (sensitivity 0.82, specificity 0.82).
population: patients with Parkinson's disease vs controls; neuromelanin-sensitive MRI studies

title: Subcortical volumetric abnormalities in bipolar disorder.
finding: Smaller hippocampal and amygdala volumes and enlarged lateral ventricles in bipolar I disorder versus controls; no significant BD-I vs BD-II volume differences.
population: ENIGMA Bipolar Disorder Working Group meta-analysis

title: Cortical abnormalities in bipolar disorder: an MRI analysis of 6503 individuals from the ENIGMA Bipolar Disorder Working Group.
finding: Thinner cortex in bipolar disorder with strongest effects in left pars opercularis (d=-0.29), left fusiform gyrus (d=-0.29) and left rostral middle frontal cortex (d=-0.28); longer illness duration associated with more thinning.
population: 6503 individuals, ENIGMA Bipolar Disorder Working Group

title: A quantitative meta-analysis of fMRI studies in bipolar disorder.
finding: Underactivation of inferior frontal gyrus and putamen with overactivation of limbic structures (parahippocampal gyrus, hippocampus, amygdala) in bipolar disorder; IFG underactivity most evident in mania.
population: quantitative meta-analysis of fMRI studies in bipolar disorder

title: Prefrontal, parietal, and limbic condition-dependent differences in bipolar disorder: a large-scale meta-analysis of functional neuroimaging studies.
finding: Condition-dependent functional differences in bipolar disorder: right posterior cingulate (rest), left amygdala (emotion), left superior/right inferior parietal lobules (cognition), and left medial orbitofrontal hyperactivation (cognition).
population: 5745 BD and 8023 controls across 506 neuroimaging experiments

title: The efficacy of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) for bipolar depression: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
finding: rTMS outperformed sham for bipolar depression (response OR 2.72); significant clinical response specifically for high-frequency rTMS over left DLPFC (OR 2.57).
population: 274 patients with bipolar depression (14 studies)

title: Systematic review and meta-analyses of neural structural and functional differences in generalized anxiety disorder and healthy controls using magnetic resonance imaging.
finding: Systematic review and meta-analyses report widely distributed structural and functional neural differences in GAD versus controls, limited by small samples (no single-region meta-analytic mapping asserted).
population: 85 structural, connectivity and task-based MRI studies of GAD

title: Grey matter alterations in generalized anxiety disorder: A voxel-wise meta-analysis of voxel-based morphometry studies.
journal: International journal of developmental neuroscience : the official journal of the International Society for Developmental Neuroscience
finding: Modest grey-matter alterations in left superior temporal gyrus in GAD; anxiety severity correlated with grey matter in right insula, lenticular nucleus, putamen and striatum.
population: voxel-based morphometry studies of GAD

title: Non-invasive brain stimulation in the treatment of generalized anxiety disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
finding: Non-invasive brain stimulation improved GAD symptoms versus controls (HARS scores, response, remission); cTBS and rTMS outperformed tDCS. Stimulation targets not specified in the abstract, so no region is asserted.
population: 7 randomized controlled trials of non-invasive brain stimulation for GAD

title: Cortical Abnormalities Associated With Pediatric and Adult Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: Findings From the ENIGMA Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder Working Group.
finding: Lower transverse temporal surface area and thinner inferior parietal cortex in adult OCD; thinner inferior and superior parietal cortices in pediatric OCD (d -0.10 to -0.33).
population: pediatric and adult OCD patients vs controls (ENIGMA-OCD)

title: Distinct Subcortical Volume Alterations in Pediatric and Adult OCD: A Worldwide Meta- and Mega-Analysis.
finding: Adults with OCD had smaller hippocampus (d=-0.13) and larger pallidum (d=0.16); unmedicated pediatric patients had larger thalamus (d=0.38).
population: worldwide meta- and mega-analysis of pediatric and adult OCD (ENIGMA-OCD)

title: The erring brain: Error-related negativity as an endophenotype for OCD-A review and meta-analysis.
finding: Increased error-related negativity amplitudes in OCD during response-conflict tasks (SMD -0.55), independent of symptom severity and age — a candidate endophenotype (scalp-level ERP; no atlas region asserted).
population: meta-analysis of error-related negativity studies in OCD

title: Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: A Meta-analysis of Randomized, Sham-Controlled Trials.
journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
finding: rTMS reduced Y-BOCS scores in OCD versus sham (Hedges g = 0.64); bilateral DLPFC targeting produced the largest effect.
population: 781 participants in 26 randomized sham-controlled rTMS trials

title: A Meta-Analysis of Hippocampal and Amygdala Volumes in Patients Diagnosed With Dissociative Identity Disorder.
journal: Journal of trauma & dissociation : the official journal of the International Society for the Study of Dissociation (ISSD)
finding: Bilaterally smaller hippocampi in DID (with comorbid PTSD) versus healthy controls, and smaller left hippocampus versus PTSD patients; no significant amygdala difference. Very small literature (3 studies).
population: meta-analysis pooling 3 volumetric studies of DID

title: Hippocampal and amygdalar volumes in dissociative identity disorder.
finding: Hippocampal volume 19.2% smaller and amygdala volume 31.6% smaller in DID versus healthy subjects.
population: patients with DID vs healthy subjects (single-site study)

title: Biological and clinical changes in premanifest and early stage Huntington's disease in the TRACK-HD study: the 12-month longitudinal analysis.
finding: Higher annualized rates of whole-brain and caudate atrophy in premanifest (caudate +1.37%/yr) and early HD (+2.86%/yr) versus controls, with grey- and white-matter atrophy even far from predicted onset.
population: 116 premanifest, 114 early-HD and 115 controls (TRACK-HD, 12-month longitudinal)

title: Onset and progression of pathologic atrophy in Huntington disease: a longitudinal MR imaging study.
finding: Caudate volume differences detectable ~14 years before motor onset; caudate atrophy rates ~10-fold higher than controls, with accelerating ventricular enlargement.
population: longitudinal MR imaging of HD patients and controls

title: Regional cortical thinning in preclinical Huntington disease and its relationship to cognition.
finding: Regionally selective cortical thinning in preclinical Huntington's disease, semi-independent of striatal volume loss and correlated with cognitive performance (specific regions not named in the abstract).
population: presymptomatic carriers of the HD mutation

title: Alpha-theta border EEG abnormalities in preclinical Huntington's disease.
finding: Reduced relative EEG power at the theta-alpha border (7-8 Hz) in preclinical HD; spectral shifts correlated with CAG repeat number and disease burden (scalp-level; no atlas region asserted).
population: preclinical carriers of the HD mutation vs controls

title: Subcortical brain volume differences in participants with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder in children and adults: a cross-sectional mega-analysis.
finding: Smaller accumbens (d=-0.15), amygdala (-0.19), caudate (-0.11), hippocampus (-0.11) and putamen (-0.14) in ADHD, with largest effects in children — consistent with delayed maturation; no pallidum or thalamus differences.
population: 1713 participants with ADHD and 1529 controls, 23 sites (ENIGMA-ADHD)

title: Brain Imaging of the Cortex in ADHD: A Coordinated Analysis of Large-Scale Clinical and Population-Based Samples.
finding: Lower cortical surface area in children with ADHD (mainly frontal, cingulate, temporal; total surface area d=-0.21) and lower fusiform and temporal pole thickness; no differences in adolescents or adults.
population: children, adolescents and adults with ADHD (ENIGMA-ADHD + Generation-R)

title: A decade of EEG Theta/Beta Ratio Research in ADHD: a meta-analysis.
finding: Elevated theta/beta ratio is not a reliable diagnostic marker of ADHD (heterogeneous effects, driven partly by changing control-group values), though a subgroup deviates and TBR may have prognostic value (scalp-level; no atlas region asserted).
population: 1253 children/adolescents with ADHD and 517 without (9 studies)

title: Neural correlates of executive function and attention in children with ADHD: An ALE meta-analysis of task-based functional connectivity studies.
finding: Hypoactivation in frontoparietal network, putamen, insula, cingulate and middle temporal gyrus with hyperactivation in occipital regions, middle frontal gyrus and parahippocampal gyrus in children with ADHD.
population: children with ADHD; ALE meta-analysis of task-based studies

title: Efficacy and Safety of Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation for Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
finding: TMS improved inattention (SMD -0.94) and hyperactivity/impulsivity (SMD -0.98) versus non-TMS interventions, persisting at 1-month follow-up for inattention; only minor adverse events. Targets not named in the abstract, so no region is asserted.
population: 325 ADHD patients in 8 studies

title: Diagnostic performance of neuromelanin-sensitive magnetic resonance imaging for patients with Parkinson's disease and factor analysis for its heterogeneity: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
finding: Neuromelanin-sensitive MRI of substantia nigra discriminated PD from controls with pooled sensitivity 89% and specificity 83%.
population: 403 PD patients vs 298 controls (12 studies)
